hero.filename: Grizzly Skull Comparison, Denver Museum of Nature and Science.jpg
hero.caption: Comparison of Colorado and Alaska Grizzly Bear Skulls, Denver Museum of Nature and Science. The Left skull is from Colorado's last known Grizzly Bear, killed in Self-Defence in the San Juan Mountains in 1979. The Right skull belongs to one of the two Alaskan Brown Bears located in the Unimak Island diorama, which the skulls are located next to.
hero.alt: Comparison of Colorado and Alaska Grizzly Bear Skulls, Denver Museum of Nature and Science. The Left skull is from Colorado's last known Grizzly Bear, killed in Self-Defence in the San Juan Mountains in 1979. The Right skull belongs to one of the two Alaskan Brown Bears located in the Unimak Island diorama, which the skulls are located next to.

images.filename: Auriferous volcanic breccia (Little Annie Mine, Summitville Mining District, San Juan Mountains, Colorado, USA) 1 (16424612663).jpg
images.caption:
Auriferous volcanic breccia from Colorado, USA. (public display, Denver Museum of Nature & Science, Denver, Colorado)
This fantastically gold-rich rock comes from Colorado's Little Annie Mine in the San Juan Mountains.  The 114 pound boulder has an estimated 316 troy ounces of native gold.  The lithology hosting the gold is a porous volcanic breccia of Tertiary age.

Locality: loose boulder along Little Annie Mine, just below the Little Annie Mine, Summitville Mining District, San Juan Mountains, Colorado, USA
images.alt:
